parsed.why: Excellent visitor-facing legal framework (self-ID, ID markers, court protections), but patterned lethal violence: ~13 trans killings in Q1 2025, armed-group kill lists in two departments. State protects but cannot prevent killings; conflict zones pull the score down.

National birth-sex bathroom law is a universal, unremedied tier-1 exposure, plus repealed hate-crime coverage and rising hate crimes. Offset by courts striking an anti-equality decree and a historic police-torture conviction; no trans criminalisation.

Visitors report little direct hostility; highest court struck workplace bathroom exclusion and the sterilisation requirement. But no gender-identity discrimination statute, family-register custody placement, documented among-men pretrial detention, and onsen friction leave real institutional exposure.

State-tolerated police targeting: mass raids with beatings, forced exams and blackmail (2017, again 2023), inadequate investigation of a trans murder, 77% hostile media, zero legal protection, ranked last regionally. Tier-2 targeting with no recourse.

Statutory trans rights, self-ID documents, trans person chooses prison placement, murder prosecuted to sentence, strong freedom index. Enforcement uneven in some services; resident violence prevalence doesn't chiefly reach visitors. No universal visitor-facing restriction documented.
